mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has declined for four consecutive weeks (-18.3 to -26.0), indicating a self-reinforcing contraction in discretionary outings. Absent a reversal signal elsewhere, this negative momentum should persist, producing a further mean decline over the next 28 days relative to the last 28 days.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC fell monotonically each of the last 4 weeks
failure_condition: If mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days despite no reversal in the weekly trend, the momentum-continuation mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility collapsed from +10.9 to -24.6 over three weeks, a sharp behavioral withdrawal from outdoor/public spaces. Once this drop exceeds a threshold magnitude, it signals a broader retreat from non-essential outings that spills over into retail and recreation visits within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls more than 30 points within a 3-week span
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS dropped from +10.9 at t-3w to -24.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC stabilizes or rises over the next 2 weeks despite PARKS crossing the -30 point cumulative decline threshold, the behavioral spillover mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in RETAIL_REC, PARKS, and TRANSIT alongside a rising RESIDENTIAL series are consistent with a tightening-restrictions regime in which public health or administrative measures are curbing non-essential mobility. Under this regime, RETAIL_REC should continue falling over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose from 3.1 to 3.9 while RETAIL_REC and TRANSIT fell concurrently
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days while RESIDENTIAL remains elevated or increasing, the tightening-restrictions regime explanation is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The joint trajectory of TRANSIT (declining steadily) and WORKPLACES (roughly flat near -13) suggests commuters are shifting away from transit for essential trips but maintaining workplace attendance, implying trip-chaining retail stops tied to transit use are being lost even though overall work activity is stable. This interaction should depress RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT fell from -14.1 to -17.3 while WORKPLACES stayed near -13 to -17
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises over the next 2 weeks while TRANSIT continues to fall and WORKPLACES remains flat, the trip-chaining interaction mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The sharp PARKS decline from +10.9 to -24.6 likely reflects late-winter seasonal weather suppressing outdoor activity rather than a durable behavioral shift. As seasonal conditions improve toward early spring, outdoor-adjacent retail and recreation activity should partially recover over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:decision date is 2022-03-15, consistent with a late-winter-to-spring seasonal transition
regime_hint: late winter to early spring transition
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC continues to decline over the next 28 days even as PARKS stabilizes or recovers seasonally, the seasonal-rebound mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has steadily declined from 7.7 to 1.9, suggesting reduced errand-bundling trips that previously co-occurred with retail visits. As this essential-trip baseline normalizes downward, the ancillary retail visits bundled with grocery runs should also fall within one week.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM fell from 7.7 at t-3w to 1.9 at t-0w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises over the next week despite continued decline in GROCERY_PHARM, the errand-bundling mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT mobility crosses a critical threshold of decline, it likely signals an active policy-driven reduction in public transport capacity or advisories against transit use, which would immediately suppress retail trips reliant on transit access within the following week.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT declined from -14.1 to -17.3 over the snapshot, approaching -20
failure_condition: If TRANSIT crosses -20 but RETAIL_REC does not fall within the following week, the transit-threshold policy mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The combination of rising RESIDENTIAL mobility and stable WORKPLACES mobility suggests a hybrid-work pattern where people remain home more during non-work hours even as job attendance holds steady, reducing discretionary trips to retail and recreation venues over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose from 3.1 to 3.9 while WORKPLACES stayed near -13 to -17
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises over the next 2 weeks while RESIDENTIAL stays elevated and WORKPLACES remains flat, the hybrid-work interaction mechanism is rejected.
